program: Food-benefit navigation, outreach and school-food policy
priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost against SNAP service benefits; not full policy portfolio or marginal-gift expected value.

what: Hunger Free Colorado connects households to food resources through a multilingual hotline, outreach and statewide partners.
It also organizes and advocates on school meals and food policy, whose benefits are not automatically counted as its own.
A conditional health-plus-net-transfer service reference is about $4.72M per better life.
strengths: The latest original filing identifies a matched annual application-household envelope.
Current service routes and local-versus-statewide boundaries are explicit.
Full public-payer transfer losses and applicant burdens are retained alongside household benefits.
reservations: HFC and partners submitted applications; these are not unique new approvals or recipient-only causal effects.
Local utility, net food resources, eligibility and additionality remain judgments.
Full recipient expenses cover policy and organizing beyond the limited service reference.

sections.what: Hunger Free Colorado, EIN 68-0551464, operates a multilingual food hotline, bilingual mobile outreach and partner network, alongside school-food advocacy. It is not the distinct Food Justice for All entity. Own donation page embeds an EveryAction form; its endpoint returned HTTP200, with no transaction made.
sections.monitoring: The original FY June2025 filing reports online SNAP applications for more than17,357 households submitted by HFC and partners. Thirty thousand individual connections are not added to this household count. Request unique approvals, continued receipt, HFC versus partner contribution, Denver residence, alternative application access and actual net resources. Current eligibility changes can alter reachable capacity; descriptive applications are not proof of treatment or improved nutrition.
sections.qualitative: Food assistance may improve food security and health, but neither submitted applications nor school-meal access establishes local causal utility. The reference uses .15 combined recipient/partner versus alternative-provider additionality, .6 resource receipt, .3 health-compatible share, .2 response and .01 utility for one year as judgments. County self-application and other navigators are alternatives. School-food, farmer and cafeteria-worker effects remain unknown, not zero; no gross wages or statewide population multiplied by a slogan.
sections.cost: FY June2025 full annual cost is $5,030,480: $5,007,591 functional expenses plus $22,889 netted fundraising expenses. Comparable FY2024 $5,550,876 and FY2023 $6,295,996 give mean $5,625,784. Recognized client-services expense $3,008,512 is an annual channel sensitivity without fully allocated overhead, not a marginal gift. Whole annual cost against a limited SNAP service channel is conservative on omitted benefits but not whole-portfolio EV. The59.6MB2025 annual report exceeded web retrieval limits and was not reviewed; matched original IRS native narrative was read.
sections.funding: Judged $2,000 net annual constrained food-consumption resources are after other-benefit withdrawal and offsets, not retail charity value or healthcare billing. Positive gains are overlap-adjusted to .6; full $10 applicant time/access costs and stress remain even failed applications. Same-household gains and costs share a joint log. Distinct taxpayer households lose the full $2,000 per changed household without positive-overlap discount; local incidence is applied once. Lower-income recipient and payer consumption baselines are judgments. Public implementation, coalition attribution, finite policy delay and job/displacement effects need separate review before wider policy benefits are added. Current donor-dependent capacity is unmeasured.

model.costScope: Whole annual FY2025 recipient cost against conditional limited SNAP-navigation benefits; recognized client-services and full-year mean sensitivities, no marginal capacity price.
model.geographicAttribution: Statewide network; g .45 judged beneficiary share in Denver's ten-county CBSA19740, not headquarters or all-Colorado attribution. Recipient and payer incidence localized once.
model.formula: Health = N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted T × g minus full exposed harm. Joint net household food resources minus access costs logged once; distinct public payer loses full transfer resources localized once. Price=10C/(health + signed resource equivalents).
model.counterfactual: County self-application, public agencies, statewide partners and other navigators may obtain benefits without Hunger Free Colorado.
model.attribution: b .15 jointly represents recipient contribution within the partner network and additional access versus alternatives, not observed successful attribution. Resource receipt distinct from health response.
model.uncertainty: Conditional initial reference, not measured causal EV. Unique current approvals, local consumption/utility, partner attribution, public payer cost and gift capacity unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2025 original filing more than17,357 application households across HFC plus partners and30,000 food-resource individual connections; not completed clinical outcomes. Organizing participants and statewide school benefits not added.
